question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-2{x}^{2}+96}$ at the point where $x=4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-2{x}^{2}+96.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (-4x) \\  & =-\frac{4x}{2\sqrt{-2{x}^{2}+96}} \\  & =-\frac{2x}{\sqrt{-2{x}^{2}+96}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & ={(-\frac{2x}{\sqrt{-2{x}^{2}+96}})|}_{x=4} \\  & =\frac{-4(4)}{2\sqrt{-2(4{)}^{2}+96}} \\  & =\frac{-16}{2\sqrt{64}} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
